teaser.en: Its black seeds wear bright red-orange caps, strung into necklaces, while its termite-proof poles hold up the main frame of a house.

summary.en: *Mbambakofi*, the pod mahogany, is a large spreading tree of dry coastal forest and the Shimba Hills, prized as one of the most important timber trees known to Digo carpenters. Logging has made it rare outside protected areas.

about.en:
*Mbambakofi* is a large, spreading tree that loses some of its leaves in the dry season. Its leaves are compound, with three to seven pairs of glossy leaflets.

The pods are its best-known feature: thick, flat and woody, splitting open to show shiny black seeds, each topped with a bright red-orange cap called an aril. The seeds stay on the tree and on the ground long after the pods have opened, and children collect them.

where.en: It grows in lowland dry forest, *Brachystegia* woodland and thicket on the coastal plain and in the Shimba Hills. Large trees are now mostly found in protected forests and kayas, where they have been spared from logging.

uses.en:
The wood is heavy, strong and handsome, used for doors, furniture and building. Its poles are very hard and resist termites, so they are chosen for the main supports of a house. Larger trunks have been used to make canoes and dhows.

The bright seeds are strung as necklaces. The tree gives shade, and it is also used in medicine.

culture.en: Pakia lists *mbambakofi* among the most important local sawn-timber trees known to Digo carpenters.

names.en: Pakia and Maundu and Tengnäs give the Digo name *mbambakofi*, which is also the Swahili name and the headword in the Mgombato dictionary. Mgombato glosses it as lucky-bean tree, pod mahogany or mahogany tree, and lists many other names from the region, including *mbaria*, *mbarikia*, *mkongo*, *mkola* and *mtame*. In Giriama it is *mwamba*. In English it is the pod mahogany or mahogany bean, and its scientific name is *Afzelia quanzensis*.

conservation.en: It is becoming rare outside protected areas because of logging.

reason.en: Grows with it in Brachystegia woodland
